newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea seen intervening in won/dlr trading.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea seen intervening in won/dlr trading.

text.p: The Bank of Korea was seen heavily selling dollars in the afternoon session on Wednesday to support the local currency, dealers said.
The won was trading at 843.90 before the dollar selling pushed the currency to an intraday high of 842.70, dealers said.
Officials at the central bank could not immediately be reached for comment.
"I think about $100 million flew into the market," said one dealer.
The local currency has been under pressure from the continued slump in the nation's exports, while imports have been rising steadily, dealers said.
The won later settled back to 843.20.
